comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C14-C16, C19, C40-C41. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the experimental data and mechanistic interpretation, while peer reviewers confirm findings are 'clear and very well presented' but note overlap with Hinz et al. 2015, questioning novelty rather than validity.

Perfect agreement on methodological claims C63-C73. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes standard techniques with proper replication, peer reviewers state 'experiments are very nicely performed and presented' and 'work was performed to a high standard.'

Strong agreement on background/contextual claims (C1-C2, C7-C13, C17-C18, C20-C21, C33, C43-C44, C46-C48, C58). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. These are established facts from literature that neither evaluation challenges.

Both address 5S vs 601 comparison (C26-C32) and breathing mechanism (C3, C31). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing strong support for breathing model. Peer review evaluates as UNCERTAIN, questioning generalizability beyond single gRNA/target combination and requesting position-independent sequence evaluation.

Both address dCas9 binding to naked DNA vs nucleosomes (C22, C25). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with reasonable interpretation. Peer review also SUPPORTED, accepting 'chromatin blocks Cas9 from binding PAM sites' as convincing and novel, though questioning broader significance.

Both address super-shift interpretation (C23-C24). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, calling interpretation 'reasonable given high number of PAMs.' Peer review evaluates as UNCERTAIN, describing it as 'curious, non-specific binding' that 'obscures results' and limits conclusions about specific vs non-specific binding.

Both address SNF2h remodeling effects (C34-C36, C42, C49, C74, C76, C78). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with consistent quantification. Peer review (R4) evaluates as UNCERTAIN, questioning what is learned beyond position-dependent cleavage and requesting deeper analysis including cleavage during (not after) remodeling.

OpenEval R5 addresses RSC remodeling (C37-C39, C42, C50, C75, C77) evaluated as SUPPORTED. Peer R4 addresses both SNF2h and RSC remodeling experiments (includes C5, C38-C39, C50, C75, C77) evaluated as UNCERTAIN, noting analysis 'is not assessed in depth.'

Both address central model and in vivo extrapolation (C51-C53). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, noting model is 'well-supported by biochemical data' though lacking direct in vivo validation. Peer review also SUPPORTED for breathing mechanism (C45-C46) but requests reconciliation with published heterochromatin studies.

Both address design recommendations and applications (C56, C59-C61). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, noting recommendations are 'logical inferences' and 'well-justified by data' though representing suggested applications. Peer review evaluates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning whether model predicts in vivo editing activity or explains published efficiency differences.

Both address speculative claims (C54-C55, C57, C62). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are 'explicitly speculative' and 'lack direct experimental support.' Peer review also UNCERTAIN, questioning in vivo relevance and requesting validation against published data or new cellular experiments.

Minor overlap on breathing mechanism claim C45. OpenEval R3 evaluates breathing model as SUPPORTED. Peer R5 also accepts breathing interpretation without challenge, stating 'Presumably due to DNA breathing' as consistent with data.
